requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints`.

**Obligations derived from the subject**
1. Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding. Whitespace-separated words are hashed individually and whitespace itself is never hashed, so `ab cd` differs from `abcd`.
2. The fingerprint scheme identifies the YAML hashing rules and their version.
3. Comments are excluded from structural hashes.

**Test mapping**
- **Comments excluded.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a YAML case on selector `pair[a]`.
  - Changing the text of an own-line comment and of a trailing comment leaves the hash unchanged.
  - Removing both comments also leaves the hash unchanged.
  - Changing a real value (`b: 1` to `b: 2`) changes the hash, so comment exclusion is not just a hash that ignores everything.
- **Words, whitespace and comments.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a YAML case on `pair[a]`.
  - Changing the comment and turning `"two words"` into `"two   words"` leaves the fingerprint equal. This shows whitespace is not hashed and comments are excluded.
  - Turning `"two words"` into `"twowords"` changes it. This shows word boundaries are preserved.
  - The same test checks that the hash value is 64 hex characters, which fits a SHA-256 digest.
- **Scheme.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts that `languages::Yaml` reports `fingerprint_scheme()` equal to `"yaml-structural-v1"`. It also asserts that `L::default()` reports the same scheme and that the loaded `OutlineContent` retains it.
- **SHA-256 specifically.** The YAML tests only check the length and hex form of the digest. A known-vector check does exist in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. It uses the standard SHA-256 empty vector and a tagged, length-prefixed token. The hashing is done by the single `Encoder` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/hash.rs`, which feeds a `Sha256` hasher. `requirements.references.structural_hash` applies the same rule in every language, so that vector covers YAML too.

**Cited requirements.** The subject cites `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` as context. The YAML-specific application of both is exercised by the tests above. I did not reassess their own tests.

I found no gap and no acknowledging {fixme}.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
